column3: PT-A05-041 matches the registered OpenAPI, Swagger UI and ReDoc handlers (FastAPI's own, by module and qualified name) and reports their route paths, instead of BootUI's fixed prefix list /v3/api-docs, /v2/api-docs, /swagger-ui, /graphiql. Reason: the Java prefixes name Spring libraries; paths are configurable in FastAPI, so the handler is the stable fact. A documentation route served by a host's own handler is not recognised, and a declared OpenAPI URL with no recognised handler is a stated gap.
The GraphiQL marker is dropped. Reason: a GraphQL library serves its IDE and its API on one route; the route table cannot distinguish them.

PT-A05-041 target is Application route table (BootUI: Spring MVC mappings); the recommendation and the learn-more link name FastAPI's conditional OpenAPI guidance and omit the H2 sentence; id, title, category, severity and confidence are BootUI's. Reason: the H2 console has no Python equivalent and there is no Spring MVC.

PT-A05-044 evaluates uvicorn.middleware.proxy_headers.ProxyHeadersMiddleware on the application stack (root and mounted) instead of server.forward-headers-strategy; its title is ProxyHeadersMiddleware trusts X-Forwarded-* headers, its target ProxyHeadersMiddleware, its evidence names the root application and each mount, and its recommendation is BootUI's with the Spring and Tomcat names replaced; id, category, severity and confidence are BootUI's. Reason: the Spring property does not exist; uvicorn's server flags are not observable and are stated in the third standing sentence.

An exception or a missing introspector method from the route read gives BootUI's endpoint gap, a partial scan and, with no A02 finding, A02 INDETERMINATE; unavailable security facts, a non-FastAPI host or any facts limitation gives BootUI's configuration gap and a partial scan, PT-A05-044 unevaluated and documentation still reported. Reason: BootUI's failed provider is truncated and its absent provider silent; here every unreadable evidence fails closed because FastAPI internals vary by version and a wrapped mount is visible only as limitation text.

Documentation route paths and mount paths in the PT-A05-041 and PT-A05-044 evidence pass through the context masker one by one before the 240-character cut and become [masked] under METADATA_ONLY; BootUI masks nothing here. Fixed text is never masked. Reason: safety model 3, same rule as pentesting:cors-evidence-masking.

Sharpit labels A07 coverage NOT_APPLICABLE where BootUI labels the same branch HANDOFF; the behaviour is ported (the hand-off branch precedes the indeterminate branch), so endpoint truncation leaves A07 unchanged and the ported assertion of PentestingScannerTests.truncatedEndpointMetadataMakesA07IndeterminateButNotA04 changes from INDETERMINATE to NOT_APPLICABLE. Reason: the BootUI test runs with Spring metadata present; sharpit has none, so its A07 is the hand-off branch.

Gaps are entries of evidence.limitations with BootUI's wording; the scan message stays fixed text and usable stays the GET probe's usability; this lane adds one new string and no standing entry because the measured worst case already uses 19 of the 20 unique entries and every promised statement must stay. Reason: BootUI appends gaps to its scan message and ORs per-check usability; sharpit's message, usable and cap are the pentesting report's.

A mount wrapped in ProxyHeadersMiddleware, absent security facts and a non-FastAPI host give BootUI's configuration gap through a boolean on the facts' limitations; the limitation text is never read. Reason: the introspector records a wrapped mount only as text, the boolean is shared with the session checks, and the text can carry a mount label.
The 4096-pattern inspection bound and its gap text are BootUI's; the 64-handler-mapping bound has no analogue. Reason: Starlette has one route tree, not a list of handler mappings.
htmlMappingsPresent is not ported. Reason: it only gates BootUI's Spring whitelabel 404 exclusion, which the scan does not apply (pentesting:browser-document).

PT-A05-016, PT-A05-019, PT-A05-027, PT-A05-028, PT-A05-032, PT-A05-033, PT-A05-034, PT-A05-035, PT-A05-036, PT-A05-037, PT-A05-038, PT-A05-039, PT-A05-049, PT-A05-052, PT-A05-053, PT-A05-054, PT-A05-055, PT-A05-056. Reason: there is no management-endpoint model in FastAPI or Starlette.
PT-A05-040. Reason: BootUI binds it to the Actuator base path; a prometheus_client ASGI app is an opaque mount at a host-chosen path, not a framework convention.
PT-A05-017. Reason: there is no embedded database console.
PT-A05-029. Reason: it is a Spring property; generic CORS is evaluated by the CORS checks.
PT-A05-051. Reason: there is no application-level request-detail logging toggle; server logging verbosity is outside the app object and a logger level is process-global state a read must not change.
PT-A05-062. Reason: there is no remote-restart secret; the Werkzeug debugger is not visible on the app object.
PT-A05-042. Reason: Starlette has no request firewall.
PT-A05-043. Reason: there is no separate management port.
PT-A07-001, PT-A07-002, PT-A07-003, PT-A07-004, PT-A07-005, PT-A01-001. Reason: Spring Security is not ported.

PT-A07-006 is covered by the security advisor's SEC-OAUTH-004 and SEC-OAUTH-006, which exempt loopback hosts and are production-only; BootUI flags any http:// issuer. Reason: the scheme-URL facts already exist in the security advisor; no pentesting finding is added.
PT-A07-007. Reason: the OAuth2 flow type is not captured by the introspector.
PT-A08-001. Reason: JVM serialization.
Flask documentation routes and the Werkzeug debugger are not checked. Reason: the pentesting scan as a whole is wired to the FastAPI adapter only.
